# <span id="aanchor62"></span> Exception Resolver

## Settings

The Exception Resolver Settings screen contains several configuration options to help you organize and access exception data. Click the gear icon 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="vertical-align: text-top;width: 18;height: 17;" /> on the main toolbar to access the Settings screen. The following options are available:

<span id="Preferences"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="User Preferences">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />User Preferences</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="User Preferences">

The User Preferences screen contains options for configuring the following:

- **Date Selector** - Select a date range display option for exception data:
  - **Current Month** - Display data from the first day of the month at 00 hours to the current date and next hour.
  - **Previous Month** – Display data from the first day of the previous month at 00 hours to first day of current month at 00 hours.
  - **Both Current and Previous Month** – Display data from the first day of previous month at 00 hours to current date and next hour.

- **Status Filter** - Select statuses to filter exceptions by.

- **Load exceptions when window opens** - Enable this option to automatically populate exceptions upon entering the Exception Resolver based on the settings you have defined. When this option is disabled, you will need to click the Refresh button to populate the exceptions list based on your settings.

- **Color detail rows** - Enable this option to color the rows in the exception grid based on status.

  

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 546;height: 124;" />

- **System** - Select a system associated with the exceptions you want to view.

- **List** - Specify a default list for the Exception Resolver. These options vary based on the system selected.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 431;height: 323;" />

</div>

<span id="Selector"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Column Selector">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Column Selector</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Column Selector">

Use the Column Selector to specify which columns to display in the Exception Resolver grid.

<div class="procedure">

To modify columns: 

- Drag and drop items from the Available Columns list to the Current Columns list, or vice versa. The order of the columns will dictate the order in which the columns display on the grid. While dragging a column into either list, a pop-up will indicate the position of the column in the list it is going into.
- Click **Select All** to move all columns to the Current Columns list.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 431;height: 323;" />

Required columns (such as Description, Exception Count and Status) cannot be removed from the Current Columns list. Device Name and Device Number are conditionally required; you can remove one or the other from the Current Columns list, but not both. If a column cannot be removed, a pop-up will display.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 435;height: 325;" />

You can also change the order of the columns by dragging and dropping column headings within the grid itself, or remove columns by dragging and dropping them outside of the grid, but FLOWCAL will not save that layout when you exit the Exception Resolver.

</div>

</div>

<span id="Grouping"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Grouping Selector">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Grouping Selector</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Grouping Selector">

Use the Grouping Selector to specify groupings for the Exception Resolver grid.

<div class="procedure">

To modify groupings:

- Drag and drop items from the Available Groupings list to the Current Groupings list, or vice versa. While dragging a column into either list, a pop-up will indicate the position of the column in the list it is going into.
- Click **Select All** to move all columns to the Current Groupings list.

The order of the columns dictates the sort order. By default, the grouping is by Device Number, Description, and then Status.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 431;height: 323;" />

Not all columns from the Exception Resolver grid are available for grouping. Those columns will not display in the Grouping Selector. If a column cannot be removed, a pop-up will display.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 438;height: 329;" />

</div>

</div>

#### Apply Changes

Click **Done** when you are ready to apply your changes to the Exceptions Resolver. If you click the close button 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 23;height: 11;" />, a dialog box will display, prompting you to save the changes. Three options are available:

- **Yes** - Save the changes and apply the settings to the Exception Resolver.
- **No** - Discard the changes and close the Settings window.
- **Cancel** - Return to the Settings window and make changes as needed. Clicking the close button will also perform this function.
